b7719b7025.q: What are the key themes and takeaways from Walter Isaacson's biography of Steve Jobs?
b7719b7025.a: Steve Jobs' team invented a name for his most important skill called the reality distortion field. The Apple name was chosen for a very specific reason. And Apple didn't make Steve Jobs a billionaire—Pixar did. The book is the most detailed and accurate account of the life of the man who created Apple, and it's a must-read for anyone who aspires to do any kind of entrepreneurial project.

b44a9d4044.q: What is Walter Isaacson's background and career before becoming a full-time biographer?
b44a9d4044.a: Walter was born in New Orleans, Louisiana in 1952. He graduated from Harvard and Pembroke College in Oxford. He started his writing career at the Sunday Times in London, eventually becoming Time Magazine's editor in 1996. After a brief period as the chairman and CEO of CNN in the early 2000s, he became president of the nonprofit organization Aspen Institute, a position he has held for over 15 years. He is also a professor of history at Tulane University in New Orleans.
